apps.name: gno.land blog
apps.description: The official blog, rendered on chain. Posts are published by an admin through the realm rather than by a deploy.

apps.name: Boards2
apps.description: The discussion forum: threads, reposts and replies, grouped into boards that are each self governed. A board is either invite only or open, and an open board asks a poster to hold a minimum GNOT balance (3000 by default) instead of an invite.

apps.name: Kourt
apps.description: Fact staking: buy a court's own coin on a bonding curve, stake it YES or NO on a claim, and earn newly minted coin plus standing for being right. The stake itself is locked rather than transferred, so it always returns 1x; only an answer or dispute bond can lose money. This is the generation kourt.xyz serves, and it is one way: payments are burned and there is no redemption.

apps.name: Kourt v3
apps.description: The second live generation of the same design, founded two way: a tenth of each payment burns and the rest is held as that court's reserve, which Redeem pays out against pro rata. Court coin is transferable here, and wrappable for a DEX. Deployed 2026-09-19; kourt.xyz still serves the v1 realm above.

apps.name: wugnot
apps.description: Wrapped GNOT: the GRC20 form of the native coin, so realms that speak the token interface can hold it.

apps.name: GnoSwap
apps.description: Concentrated-liquidity AMM. The router is the entry point, and the pool, position, staker, gns, gnft and governance realms under gno.land/r/gnoswap are the rest of the same DEX.

apps.name: GovDAO
apps.description: Chain governance: proposals, votes and the executors that change parameters under r/sys/params. The r/sys realms it writes to are listed below as parts of it rather than as separate apps.

apps.name: Params
apps.description: The chain's parameter store, and the thing GovDAO proposals actually write to. The transfer lock, the code submission policy, run_submitters, the halt height, the validator set and fee collection all read their value from here.

apps.name: Valopers
apps.description: The validator registry. Operators register here and edit their own description, so a moniker is self-declared.

apps.name: Users
apps.description: The on-chain username registry. It is what resolves a @handle to an address across the explorer, and r/sys/namereg is the realm anyone registers one in.

apps.name: Bubble Rumble
apps.description: Last bid standing takes the pot. A bid pushes the pool's clock out and splits itself between the pot, the pool's earlier bidders, whoever invited the bidder, the pool's creator and the BUBBLE treasury, settled by a flag war on the pool's last day. A bid may also carry a shot at popping the bubble early, drawn by a keeper's commit-reveal. The realm renders the current split itself, which is why none of it is quoted here.

apps.name: moul's blog
apps.description: A personal blog that is a realm: one author, and posts that live in chain storage rather than in the code. Writing one is a single Set transaction, so publishing never redeploys and never costs a deploy.

apps.name: moul's home
apps.description: A profile page that is a realm. gnoweb builds /u/moul by calling Render on the realm at exactly r/<username>/home and embedding the result, so the page is whatever this realm decides to print.

apps.name: Gnogolf
apps.description: Free 3D mini-golf in the browser: every hole is data published on chain, anyone can add holes of their own, and the realm computes every shot, so nobody can fake a score. Playing needs no wallet; recording a round is a transaction, and only players with a gno.land name are ranked.

apps.name: Connect 4
apps.description: Staked Connect 4: both players put up the same GNOT and the winner takes the pot, minus the house fee each offer fixes when it is posted. Who moves first is drawn from a two-sided commit-reveal, so neither player can rig the start, and every move runs on a 90 second clock that anybody may settle once it expires. The board is playable in gnoweb, where each move is a transaction you sign; the arcade front-end plays it with a session key instead, which may only move, reveal, claim a timeout or cancel.

apps.name: Memba Feed
apps.description: The open social feed behind Memba: any wallet may post, with no membership gate and no funds held by the realm. An author soft-deletes their own posts and anyone may sweep the tombstones; open writing is kept usable by a per-address cooldown that is stricter for young accounts, a daily flag budget, and a flag threshold that hides a post automatically.

apps.name: Memba Reviews
apps.description: Ratings and reviews for anything the chain can name: a validator, a candidate, an address, or an org's realm path. One editable review per wallet per subject, plus likes, one level of replies and flags, and an author's net likes as a running reputation. The text is permanent on chain, and hiding a review only omits it from reads.

apps.name: Memba Quests
apps.description: Turns a Memba quest completion and the XP it earned into a fact anyone can check. The backend signs a voucher with a key that never touches the chain, the player broadcasts it and pays the gas, and the realm verifies the signature, refuses a reused nonce and records the XP. The signature is the authority rather than the caller, so there is no hot server key that can write here.

apps.name: vik telescope
apps.description: A real smart telescope, driven from the chain and publishing what it sees. Its owner grants an address access for a number of days, an authorised caller queues a capture by right ascension, declination and exposure, and the controller that owns the hardware pops that queue and records the resulting image back on chain. The realm renders its own status, queue and capture history, and registers itself with NightSky, the telescope network at r/nym-vikbez000/nightsky/v1.

apps.name: GnoRadio
apps.description: Community radio on chain: everyone tuned to a station hears the same track at the same second, computed from block time, with no streaming server in the middle. There is a station per genre plus the newest tracks and the ones listeners picked, and listeners can program a track into a station's schedule. Artists publish their own tracks beside openly licensed and imported ones, and a tip lands in the artist's wallet in the same transaction. This realm is the site; the catalog and radio realms hold the rules and the data realm holds every record.

Prediction markets on sport and on world events, priced in GNOT: a share in the outcome that happens pays one GNOT, and every share is fully collateralised, so a market can never owe more than it holds. Prices come from the lister's own two-sided quotes, which expire rather than hang around stale. The result comes from the oracle each market pins, and a proposed outcome waits a day, in which a guardian may cancel it, before anyone can make it final; a market nobody resolves can be voided by anyone two months after trading ends, and every holder refunded.
